headline: BHP PROFIT SURGES 30% IN FY26: COPPER OVERTAKES IRON ORE FOR FIRST TIME — 54% OF GROUP EBITDA
snippet: BHP Group reported FY2026 full-year results on August 18, with underlying attributable profit up 30% to more than US$13 billion and total Underlying EBITDA of approximately US$33 billion — driven by copper generating more than US$18 billion of EBITDA, or 54% of Group total, marking the first time in BHP's history that copper has overtaken iron ore as the primary earnings contributor. Copper production was 1,953 kilotonnes, within raised guidance. The structural significance: BHP, the world's largest miner, is now a copper-majority earnings business at a time when LME copper trades above $6.50 per pound and AI/electrification demand is rewriting long-run demand forecasts. For junior copper developers on TSX-V and ASX whose feasibility studies were modelled at $3.50-$4.00 copper, BHP generating 54% of its earnings from copper at today's prices is the most powerful possible endorsement of the commodity thesis.

headline: NEXGEN BREAKS GROUND ON $2.2B ROOK I IN SASKATCHEWAN — 30M LB/YEAR TARGET WOULD SUPPLY 20% OF GLOBAL URANIUM
snippet: NexGen Energy broke ground on the $2.2 billion Rook I uranium project in northern Saskatchewan on August 13-14, 2026 — the largest new uranium mine under active construction globally and the first significant new uranium mine construction start in Canada in decades. The Arrow Deposit is among the highest-grade uranium deposits in the world. At full capacity, Rook I targets 30 million pounds of uranium per year — representing approximately 20% of current global uranium supply and more than half of the Western world's annual output. Notable attendees: former Prime Minister Stephen Harper, Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe, and NexGen CEO Leigh Curyer. For uranium investors, Rook I moving from permitting to active four-year construction with a fully committed $2.2 billion program is the single most consequential Western uranium supply-chain development of the current cycle — directly addressing the deficit that has driven spot to $87/lb and accelerated utility long-term contracting.

headline: TERTIARY MINERALS FINDS NEW COPPER ZONE AT MUSHIMA NORTH: 25M AT 0.38% CU IN ZAMBIA — 900M OUTSIDE KNOWN RESOURCE
snippet: Tertiary Minerals (AIM: TYM) announced August 17 that scout drilling at Mushima North in Zambia has defined a new Western Zone of copper mineralisation approximately 900 metres west-southwest of the existing Discovery Zone — with pXRF analysis returning 25 metres at 0.38% copper from 19 metres, including 13 metres at 0.53% copper and a 3-metre peak of 0.75% copper at 33 metres. The new zone lies completely outside the current exploration target, which itself holds an estimated 15-30 million tonnes grading 40-60 g/t silver equivalent. A copper zone confirmed at surface-accessible depths, 900 metres from the known resource and at grades above typical open-pit cutoffs, significantly expands the Mushima North system footprint ahead of the company's targeted 2026 maiden Mineral Resource Estimate. Zambia's Copperbelt infrastructure and established mining jurisdiction reduce the development risk premium normally applied to African greenfield discoveries.

headline: GOLD HITS $4,400 AND MINERS FINALLY CATCH UP — GDX REBOUNDS AS EQUITY DISCOUNT TO BULLION COMPRESSES
snippet: 24/7 Wall St. reports August 16 that gold miner equities — persistently lagging the physical metal through the August 2026 rally — are showing signs of closing the gap, with the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) outperforming bullion on a percentage basis as investors rotate from physical ETFs into producer equities for operational leverage. GDX currently sits approximately 20% below its March 2026 all-time highs despite gold touching $4,429 today — implying the equity-to-metal discount that frustrated mining investors through 2026's consolidation phase is beginning to resolve. The Q2 2026 earnings season has confirmed record cash flows and near-record margins across major producers; when sector earnings are at record highs and valuation multiples remain below five-year averages, the gap historically closes via equity price appreciation rather than earnings deterioration.

headline: CRITICAL MINERALS BULL MARKET ARRIVES AS CHINA DEPLOYS EXPORT ARSENAL — NOVEMBER 2026 DEADLINE THE DEFINING TRIGGER
snippet: InvestorNews' August 16 critical minerals report calls the onset of a structural bull market in critical minerals, driven by China reimposing its rare earth and strategic mineral export restriction arsenal with key exemptions running only through November 10, 2026. That deadline is not routine: it is the date the West discovers whether two years of supply-chain diversification — government loan programs, DoD offtake deals, allied-nation partnerships — can absorb a full reimposition of Chinese export controls on materials essential to defence manufacturing, AI hardware, and energy infrastructure. The current bull market differs structurally from 2010-2011 because Western governments are now direct market participants through loan guarantees and procurement mandates, effectively establishing a price floor that no comparable amount of private capital could have sustained in prior cycles. For investors in antimony, gallium, germanium, graphite, and rare earth developers, November 10 is the next hard catalyst.

headline: US AND JAPAN TARGET 6,000 METRES UNDER THE PACIFIC — 16M TONNE RARE EARTH MUD FIELD NEAR MINAMITORISHIMA
snippet: The United States and Japan are advancing plans for the world's deepest undersea mine — targeting rare-earth-rich mud deposits near Minamitorishima, a remote Japanese island territory roughly 1,900 kilometres southeast of Tokyo, at depths of approximately 6,000 metres. A single deposit is estimated to hold 16 million tonnes of rare earth minerals, including enough yttrium for approximately 780 years of global demand and enough dysprosium for 730 years. In January-February 2026, Japan's JAMSTEC deep-sea drilling vessel Chikyu successfully recovered rare-earth-bearing mud from target depths, with a full-scale processing trial planned for February 2027 and a commercialisation roadmap by 2028. For investors in land-based rare earth developers, the project validates the structural supply crisis while confirming that undersea extraction at 6,000 metres — even if technically successful — is unlikely to be commercially competitive with land-based mines for at least a decade, preserving the near-term investment case for companies like MP Materials and USA Rare Earth.

headline: TOWER RESOURCES RABBIT NORTH: 18.8M AT 2.57 G/T AU IN THUNDER ZONE — HIGH-GRADE CORE 5.74 G/T OVER 7.3M IN BC
snippet: Tower Resources (TSXV: TWR) reported August 13 that the first assay results from the June diamond drilling program at Rabbit North, near Kamloops, BC, include 18.8 metres at 2.57 g/t gold — including 7.3 metres at 5.74 g/t gold and a 0.7-metre peak of 43 g/t — near the top of the Thunder Zone target. Hole 075 intersected the Rainbow porphyry breccia, returning 22.6 metres at 0.56 g/t gold and 0.35% copper, confirming a multi-target district with both high-grade lode gold and copper-gold porphyry mineralisation. Assays from five holes, totalling 568.9 metres of core from the Blue Sky and Thunder North targets, remain pending. A 2.57 g/t average over 18.8 metres in a Tier-1 BC gold program — with a high-grade core and adjacent porphyry-style intercepts — is the type of multi-zone result that attracts institutional attention at $4,429 gold.

headline: CATL SICHUAN LITHIUM MINE FACES UNCERTAIN FUTURE — KEY DOMESTIC SOURCE CLOUDS CHINA'S SELF-SUFFICIENCY PUSH
snippet: Mining Weekly reports August 14 that CATL's Sichuan lithium mining operation faces an uncertain production future, introducing a significant variable into China's strategy of building domestic lithium supply-chain depth and reducing dependence on Australian and South American concentrate imports. The uncertainty lands at a complicated juncture for Chinese lithium economics: domestic lithium carbonate prices have risen approximately 85% year-on-year as Australian producers including Mineral Resources have restarted previously idled operations, while broader capital investment in lithium mining globally fell 40% through 2025. For TSX-V and ASX lithium developers, CATL's domestic supply uncertainty provides indirect support for the thesis that non-Chinese lithium supply will be required at meaningful scale — reinforcing the case for Tier-1 jurisdiction assets whose economics now work at current spot prices.

headline: KAZATOMPROM H1 2026 URANIUM OUTPUT RISES 9% YEAR-ON-YEAR — WORLD'S LARGEST PRODUCER RAMPS AS SPOT HOLDS $87/LB
snippet: Kazatomprom, the world's largest uranium producer controlling approximately 22% of global mine output, reported this week that H1 2026 production rose 9% year-on-year — a significant supply increase from the Kazakhstan state miner that is the primary swing producer in the current cycle. The 9% Kazakhstan production growth is important context for the $87/lb spot uranium price: even with this supply response, uranium spot remains well above the long-run incentive price for new Western mine development ($55-65/lb range), implying that market balance requires either continued Kazakh growth or new mine development outside Kazakhstan. For Western uranium investors, the data reinforces a key thesis: Kazakhstan's geographic concentration and geopolitical dependencies — Russian and Chinese relationships — motivate utilities to contract with Athabasca Basin and US ISR producers regardless of marginal cost premium, because supply-chain security is the overriding procurement criterion for the next generation of nuclear reactors.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER SET UP FOR HUGE MOVE — PHYSICAL SHORTAGES, CENTRAL BANK DEMAND, AND JACKSON HOLE ALIGN FOR Q3
snippet: GoldSeek analysis argues that gold and silver are positioned for a significant Q3-Q4 2026 move, citing three converging structural drivers: persistent physical supply shortages in the London silver market with the six-consecutive-year supply deficit continuing, central bank gold accumulation running above 1,000 tonnes per year for the third consecutive year, and a Federal Reserve trajectory that makes structurally negative real rates the most likely multi-year outcome regardless of near-term FOMC decisions. The precious metals setup is distinct from prior cyclical rallies because underlying demand is institutional and sovereign rather than speculative: silver industrial demand from solar PV fabrication alone is estimated at 232 million ounces in 2026, central banks are buying at the fastest sustained pace since the 1970s, and Kevin Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole address — his first as Fed Chair — is the scheduled event most capable of either catalysing or temporarily interrupting the move. Gold at $4,429 has now exceeded the August 12 post-correction recovery high of $4,424, suggesting the corrective phase that began in late January may be fully exhausted.
